test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 09 May 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Amendment Act, 2021 increases the upper limit for termination from 20 to __________ weeks for certain categories of women.
solution:
The correct answer is __**24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Amendment Act, 2021** was passed by the Parliament of India on **March 17, 2021**.
 
• This amendment increases the upper limit for termination of pregnancy from 20 weeks to 24 weeks for certain categories of women, including rape survivors, victims of incest, and other vulnerable women such as differently-abled women and minors.
 
• This amendment was made to address the difficulties faced by women who were unable to access safe and legal abortions due to the earlier restrictive provisions of the MTP Act.
 
• The 22-week option mentioned in the question is incorrect as the upper limit has been increased to 24 weeks. The other options, 26 weeks, 28 weeks, and blank, are also incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• The MTP Act was first enacted in India in 1971 and was amended in 1975 and 2002.
 
• The earlier version of the MTP Act allowed termination of pregnancy only up to 12 weeks and required the opinion of two doctors for termination between 12 to 20 weeks.
 
• The 2002 amendment increased the upper limit for termination to 20 weeks and allowed termination up to 24 weeks in case of certain medical conditions.
 
• The 2021 amendment further relaxed the provisions of the MTP Act and increased the upper limit for termination to 24 weeks for certain categories of women.
 
• The MTP Act also provides for the establishment of registered abortion clinics and the training of medical professionals in safe and legal abortion practices.
